task_instance: Run NV-Reason-CT inference on one user-provided 3D NIfTI chest CT volume with the default structured-chest-CT-report prompt via scripts/run_nv_reason_ct.py, producing the result_json deliverable with nonempty response text (requiring exit 0, runtime.mode == hf_transformers, runtime.mock == false, not truncated).
blocker_detail: The core deliverable (real NV-Reason-CT Transformers inference emitting a report in result_json) cannot run on this offline, GPU-less workstation. (1) No CUDA-capable NVIDIA GPU: nvidia-smi is not found and the skill states CUDA is always required with bfloat16 support; the wrapper's readiness logic recommends 'use_a_cuda_host' when CUDA is unavailable. (2) The required Python ML stack is absent: importing torch, transformers, huggingface_hub, and nibabel all fail (only base Python 3.13 is present), and the wrapper never installs packages while the runtime has no network and package installation is disallowed. (3) The nvidia/NV-Reason-CT model weights and custom code must be fetched from the Hugging Face hub (the script calls huggingface_hub snapshot_download / hf_hub_download and from_pretrained); downloading model assets requires network access, which this air-gapped runtime does not provide, and no cached snapshot exists locally. Per the task's definition, anything not already installed and anything needing the network counts as a missing runtime tool. The skill's own bundled script is present, so this is not a missing-skill-file case; the blocker is the runtime's absent GPU, absent ML dependencies, and absent network for weight download.
evidence: Probed runtime in the work dir: 'python3 --version' -> Python 3.13.17; 'nvidia-smi' -> command not found (no GPU); 'python3 -c import torch' / transformers / nibabel / huggingface_hub all raise ModuleNotFoundError (none installed). Inspected the bundled wrapper at the skill path scripts/run_nv_reason_ct.py (read-only): it imports torch, transformers (AutoModelForImageTextToText, AutoProcessor), huggingface_hub (snapshot_download, hf_hub_download), nibabel and numpy; _cuda_report() uses torch.cuda.is_available()/is_bf16_supported(); readiness recommends 'use_a_cuda_host' when CUDA is absent; model loading uses from_pretrained with trust_remote_code and resolves/downloads a Hub revision. Attempting to copy and run 'run_nv_reason_ct.py --check-setup' was blocked by the external-code policy, but the missing imports mean the check-setup report would itself report dependencies unavailable and setup not ready, and inference additionally needs a GPU and a hub download. No deliverable produced beyond result.json. No sample CT was created because the inference stack (and even nibabel to write a NIfTI) is entirely absent, so the blocker stands regardless of input.
